  • Mobile view of the theme is optimized even more: important hyperlinks and buttons are enlarged; header bar layout is improved.

The only thing left to do is find some bugs or things I've overlooked. Now that the theme is finished, I can roll it out and start tweaking it for each of the default subs I was assigned to.

And, later down the road, make more themes!

Happy whoaversing, everyone!

Bell Labs tested a new technology dubbed XG-FAST - 10GB speed over copper with a max distance of 30 meters which could effectively eliminating the need to bring fiber from the street level to a house
Bell Labs tested a new technology dubbed XG-FAST - 10GB speed over copper with a max distance of 30 meters which could effectively eliminating the need to bring fiber from the street level to a house

This article seems to be saying that Bell Labs can achieve 10 Gbps over a single pair phone line? I couldn't make out if they meant 4 pair cabling or single pair. Anyrate Verizon is going to regret pulling out all of that copper.

The article is sparse on facts. But 10Gbps over only 30m, is already a simple problem to solve. And one that's already better solved by fiber. If this worked out to 1km, even if it were only 1Gb, it would be very useful. At 30m, not so much.
Alcatel Lucent's growth has been nuts in the past 5 years. We use the 7750's and 7950's utterly insane boxes capable of 400Gbps.

The last 30 meters isn't the problem, that's a trivial problem and a cheap one to solve; it's the last mile that's difficult and expensive. And this XG-Fast still needs to be fed with fiber, and not just to the pedestal (that's rarely within 30 meters) you have to go practically right outside the house. So what problem does this solve exactly?
